Brand guide and mood board · November 2026

How Jeetak looks and sounds.

Jeetak (جيتك, “I came to you”) is the delivery app of the Upper Metn: food, groceries and anything else from the restaurants and shops of 24 villages, brought to the door and paid in cash. Everything we post should feel like that knock at the door: local, warm, quick.

Brand.

Whatever you want, from your own village's shops, at your door.

Tagline

شو ما بدّك.

Shou ma baddak, “Whatever you want.” Always with the shadda on د and the full stop. It sits under the wordmark and closes captions.

English line

Everything you need.

Only where Arabic can't go: the App Store and Google Play listings, English posts and decks.

Retired

ما في؟ جيتك

The old tagline. Don't use it anywhere.

Logo.

Custom lettering with a map pin dotting the j: it says “we come to you.” Pick a lockup and a background, and the right colors follow. Never retype or rebuild it.

Lockup
Background

PNG for Canva and phone apps, SVG for print and the web. The pack has every lockup and colorway in both, plus profile pictures.

Clear space and size

x
  • Keep clear space equal to the pin's width (x) on every side.
  • Smallest sizes: wordmark 80px or 20mm, lockups 160px or 40mm, mark 24px or 6mm.
  • On a 1080px post: lockup 220–320px wide, or the mark 72–120px tall.

Don't

Color.

Orange, Spark, Pin Green and Ink come straight from the logo files. Tap a color to copy its hex.

One ground, one support, one accent

Lead with one ground over about 60% of the layout, add one supporting color (about 30%) and at most one accent (about 10%). Alternate Orange and Cream posts; save Pine for night, winter and premium moments.

Orange 60White 3010
Cream 60Ink 3010
Pine 60White 3010

Never

  • Orange text on Pine (2.8:1)
  • A Pin Green mark on Pine (1.5:1) or on Orange (1.8:1)
  • Spark and Orange side by side as two fields (1.3:1)
  • Spark for small text on White or Cream (3.2:1 and 3.1:1)
  • White for small text on Orange (4.3:1): use black

For print and fabric, give suppliers these hex values, ask for the nearest Pantone, and approve a printed or stitched proof. Orange shifts the most between screen, paper and fabric.

Contrast checker

Pick a text color and a background to see whether the pair works. “Headlines only” means 24px or more on screen, which is 72px or more on a 1080px post.

Voice.

Lebanese Arabic, written short, like a neighbor talking. Name the moment, answer with the name: «[the need]؟ جيتك.»

Headline playground

Pick a moment or write your own, then choose a ground. The post and its caption update as you go.

Moment
Ground

Caption

How we write

  • Headlines and captions in Lebanese Arabic, in Arabic script. English for store listings and English posts. Arabizi only in comments and DMs.
  • Talk to the customer as «إنت». Written «بدّك» reads as both baddak and baddik, so it speaks to everyone.
  • “Jeetak” with a capital J in sentences, «جيتك» in Arabic. Lowercase “jeetak” lives only in the logo; never “JEETAK”.
  • End headlines with a full stop. Use ؟ in Arabic text.
  • Two emoji per caption at most, never in headlines or on designs. Three hashtags at most.

RIDERS IN KIT

Avoid

  • City skylines and Beirut traffic
  • Stock photos that could be anywhere
  • Other brands' logos, bags or uniforms in frame
  • Riders out of kit
  • Text over faces, food or the logo's clear space; put it on a calm area or a Pine panel

AI images and video

  • Composite the real logo and app screens in post, onto blank surfaces.
  • Never let AI draw the logo, Arabic text, signs or app screens.
  • Keep phones dark or face-down in AI shots.
  • No on-camera Arabic dialogue in AI video: use voice-over.
  • Keep the mix at about 60% AI and 40% real footage.

Social.

One message per post: a headline of up to six words, one supporting line, one button, the logo in a bottom corner.

Stories, Reels and TikTok

1080 × 1920. Keep text out of the top 250px and the bottom 340px, where the app's own controls sit. Promote the app that fits the audience: Jeetak for customers, Jeetak Driver for riders, Jeetak Partner for shops.

Caption formula

Hook first («جوعان؟ جيتك.»), then one line on what to do, sign off with «شو ما بدّك.», then up to three hashtags.
